QQQ.source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance (unofficial provider client)

interpretation.text:
On Nov 25, QQQ’s 252-return DFA H was 0.454, below the ideal independent, finite-variance reference of 0.5. R²=0.920 measures fit only on supplied scales. Short/long estimates (0.364/0.537) show one line fits poorly across 8–63, possibly reflecting crossover or a temporary volatility shift. Magnitude H=0.757 suggests volatility clustering, not tradable predictability.

H fell 0.026/0.020 over one/five observations. Its prior-30 z-score was −1.79, not a significance test because windows overlap. H/alpha went from 0.520/3.300 (Nov 6) to 0.480/3.270 (Nov 24) to 0.454/3.331.

Hill uses 1,000 returns (~4 years), k=100, and x_min=0.02046 in absolute log-return units. Lower/higher alpha suggests heavier/thinner tails if the model fits. The idealized i.i.d. standard error, 0.333, understates uncertainty under dependence. The 5%/15% cutoffs give 3.324/3.000, not confidence bounds. Unchanged top extremes can produce normal plateaus without implying a static market. These are uncertain descriptive estimates, not a crash forecast.
